Morbstack host Docker CLI toolchain provenance
=================================================

Three Docker client-side binaries live here, laid out exactly the way
Morbstack.app itself bundles them (Contents/Resources/host-bin/) and the
way the `docker` CLI's own cli-plugins resolution expects:

    dist/host-bin/docker                        <- the client itself
    dist/host-bin/cli-plugins/docker-compose     <- `docker compose` plugin
    dist/host-bin/cli-plugins/docker-buildx      <- `docker buildx` plugin

All three are host Mac (arm64) binaries that never enter the VM/initramfs.
`docker` is the main entry point a user's shell resolves; the two plugin
binaries are resolved by that `docker` binary itself via its cli-plugins
mechanism, which is why they live one level down in a `cli-plugins/`
subdirectory rather than beside it.

Together they exist so that installing Morbstack is a complete, working
Docker CLI + engine on a Mac that has *never* had Docker Desktop, Homebrew's
`docker`, or anything else Docker-shaped installed — see docs/parity.md's
zero-config-discovery finding and docs/compat.md. `morb install-cli`
(mac/Sources/morb/main.swift) is what actually wires these onto a user's
system, always with explicit consent — see that command's own help text and
MorbstackKit/CliPlugins.swift/MorbPathSetup.swift for the mechanics.

The reserved path below is deliberately different: it is a private app helper,
not a Docker plugin and never a user-installed command. Its provenance record
is kept here before its bytes are fetched so a release pipeline has one
deterministic source of truth. A normal source checkout and the current app do
**not** contain it, and no port-forward capability is implemented or exposed.

    dist/host-bin/kubernetes/kubectl                 <- future private helper

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
docker (the client itself)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

File: docker
Version: 29.7.1 (matches dist/guest-bin/dockerd's engine version exactly —
         zero client/server skew)
Platform: darwin-arm64
License: Apache-2.0 (same as upstream docker/cli; this repo redistributes
         Docker Inc.'s client binary, unmodified, under that license — see
         the LICENSE/NOTICE/AUTHORS files inside the fetched bottle, not
         reproduced here, for the full text)
sha256: 49d98ab806e8678cd6341b09dad6389e5bcd8a46513de7651053bee3d8366e8d

Source and why it isn't a Docker Inc. release: Docker Inc. does not publish
a standalone macOS CLI-only binary through its own release infrastructure.
download.docker.com's static tarballs are Linux-only (see the docker/
dockerd/etc. entries fetched into dist/guest-bin/ from that exact source),
and the docker/cli GitHub repository has no Releases at all
(`GET /repos/docker/cli/releases/latest` -> 404, checked directly at pin
time). The only widely-used, independently-auditable build of just the
client for darwin/arm64 is Homebrew core's own `docker` formula
(https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/docker, Apache-2.0), built and bottled by
Homebrew's own CI, not by Docker Inc. and not extracted from a Docker
Desktop installer (deliberately: this project replaces Docker Desktop, so
depending on its distribution channel for even one component would be an
odd foundation).

Bottle URL:
  https://ghcr.io/v2/homebrew/core/docker/blobs/sha256:1bc0f3ce68c682ff23050b964f9a721b15fa1524ae29129c02c96d3966e98dcd
Bottle sha256 (of the whole .tar.gz, before extracting the one member kept):
  1bc0f3ce68c682ff23050b964f9a721b15fa1524ae29129c02c96d3966e98dcd
Member extracted: docker/29.7.1/bin/docker

Verification: ghcr.io blobs are content-addressed by their own sha256
digest, so the URL and the pin above are the same value by construction —
downloading and independently recomputing the hash (which
scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh's fetch_docker_cli does on every fetch) is
still a real corruption/tamper check, it just isn't a *second independent
source* the way compose/buildx's GitHub sidecar files are. As a second,
independent cross-check at pin time, the same digest was confirmed against
Homebrew's own formula API
(`https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/docker.json`, key
`.bottle.stable.files.arm64_tahoe.sha256`), which agreed exactly. The
extracted binary's own hash (above) is checked at pin time but not re-hashed
on every fetch, because the bottle also carries man pages, shell
completions, and the formula's own metadata files whose presence/absence
does not affect the shipped binary's correctness — `fetch_docker_cli`
instead checks that the installed binary runs and reports exactly
"version 29.7.1", which is the property that actually matters.

`file` confirms: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64. Ad-hoc/linker-signed.
Runs standalone (`./docker --version` -> "Docker version 29.7.1, build
e9452d6e78") on this host with no other Docker installation present.

Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--cli-only).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
docker-compose
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

File: cli-plugins/docker-compose
Source: https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/download/v5.3.1/docker-compose-darwin-aarch64
Release: docker/compose v5.3.1 (latest release at time of fetch)
Platform: darwin-aarch64 (host Mac, arm64)
License: Apache-2.0
sha256: 32691ba1196d819fa68cbdc0aad9a5569e730a35ae40c6fdd8458110ecd69488

Verification: sha256 fetched from GitHub Release's own per-asset sidecar
file (docker-compose-darwin-aarch64.sha256, published alongside the
binary in the same release) and matched the locally computed hash
exactly.

`file` confirms: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64. Runs standalone
(`./docker-compose version` -> "Docker Compose version v5.3.1") on this
host without needing `docker` on PATH first.

Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--compose-only).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
docker-buildx
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

File: cli-plugins/docker-buildx
Source: https://github.com/docker/buildx/releases/download/v0.36.0/buildx-v0.36.0.darwin-arm64
Release: docker/buildx v0.36.0 (latest release at time of fetch)
Platform: darwin-arm64 (host Mac, arm64)
License: Apache-2.0
sha256: 82c6a3d9df37790c5bdb0d7ca88986d1d17622fc2b88ebe34b275c6c47acd7a6

Verification: docker/buildx's release does NOT put darwin hashes in its
plain `checksums.txt` asset (that file only lists linux/freebsd/netbsd/
openbsd builds) — the darwin (and windows) hashes live in the separate
`checksums-signed.txt` asset for the same release instead. The pin above
was matched against that file's
"82c6a3d9...  *buildx-v0.36.0.darwin-arm64" line, and independently
cross-checked against the GitHub Releases API's own per-asset "digest"
field for that same asset (`GET /repos/docker/buildx/releases/latest`,
`assets[].digest` = "sha256:82c6a3d9..."), which agreed exactly. Both
matched the locally computed hash of the downloaded file.

`file` confirms: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64. Runs standalone
(`./docker-buildx version` -> "github.com/docker/buildx v0.36.0 ...") on
this host without needing `docker` on PATH first.

Purpose: parity check #13/#14 in docs/parity.md — the guest's dockerd
ships upstream BuildKit and it is fully functional (multi-platform
builds, cache mounts, everything works), but no `docker-buildx` client
binary was shipped anywhere in the repo, so `docker build` (BuildKit is
the default builder since Docker 23+) and `docker buildx build` both
failed out of the box with a stock docker CLI: `docker: 'buildx' is not
a docker command`. This is the single highest-ROI fix identified by that
audit. Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--buildx-only).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
kubectl (private, future selected-Pod port-forward helper)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Status: declared and verified when explicitly staged; absent from the current
bundle. This is not a general `kubectl` distribution, an installation action,
or evidence that Morbstack currently implements Kubernetes port-forwarding.

File: kubernetes/kubectl
Version: v1.36.2
Platform: darwin-arm64
License: Apache-2.0
Source: https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.36.2/bin/darwin/arm64/kubectl
sha256: 4408c85c83fd3a31adaa555bdf3c7a6c81f74b19449a9060ba31ab91926f023d

Verification: `scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh --host-kubectl-only` first
compares the official adjacent `kubectl.sha256` sidecar to the pin above, then
hashes the downloaded bytes before installing them. `mise run app` repeats the
same hash check and refuses a symlink before it copies/signs an explicitly
staged helper. `MorbKubernetesKubectl.bundledKubectl()` repeats the regular-file,
executable, and SHA-256 checks at future use time. It never searches PATH or
uses a person's kubectl, KUBECONFIG, or ~/.kube/config when the helper is absent
or invalid.

The helper lives outside `cli-plugins`, is never touched by `morb install-cli`,
and is not fetched by the script's default asset set. A later selected-Pod
coordinator must use it only through its fixed absolute bundle path and a
Morbstack-private ephemeral credential file; that coordinator and its required
clean-cluster acceptance matrix are still pending in docs/k8s.md.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Installing the toolchain
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

None of the three binaries are installed anywhere on `PATH` or into
~/.docker/cli-plugins/ by the fetch script itself — fetching is a
repo-local caching step and must not touch the user's dotfiles or shell
configuration without being asked. Two supported ways to install:

  1. `morb install-cli` — explains exactly what it will do (symlink
     `docker` into ~/.morbstack/bin/, symlink docker-compose and
     docker-buildx from here into ~/.docker/cli-plugins/), asks for
     confirmation, and does nothing without an explicit yes (or --force).
     It never shadows an existing, already-resolvable `docker` on PATH
     unless you separately opt in with `--make-default` (its own,
     separately-worded confirmation — see `morb install-cli --help`).
     `morb install-cli --print-plan` shows the plan without prompting;
     `morb install-cli --json` gives scriptable output.

  2. The manual one-liner, if you would rather do it yourself:
       mkdir -p ~/.morbstack/bin ~/.docker/cli-plugins
       ln -sf "$(pwd)/dist/host-bin/docker" ~/.morbstack/bin/docker
       ln -sf "$(pwd)/dist/host-bin/cli-plugins/docker-compose" ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose
       ln -sf "$(pwd)/dist/host-bin/cli-plugins/docker-buildx" ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx
       # then add ~/.morbstack/bin to PATH yourself, e.g. in ~/.zshrc:
       #   export PATH="$HOME/.morbstack/bin:$PATH"
